features.name: Calendar multi-view with a unified date
steps: Switch the state between the day view, week view, month view, month view + day view, year view, and simple event list
The current date stays consistent
The same event appears in all applicable views
After opening an event from a view and returning, the reasonable date context is restored
features.expected: All views must share the same date and event data source, and switching views must not jump back to today or lose the current date; the same event must appear in all applicable views; after returning from the event details the original view and date are restored.

features.name: Month and date navigation
steps: The month view switches months with the left/right arrows
The year changes correctly across year boundaries
Tap a day to enter that day's event view
Use "Go to date" to pick the year and month directly
After confirming, all views jump to the target date
features.expected: When paging months across a year boundary the year and month must link correctly (after December comes January of the next year); tapping a day must enter that day's event view; after confirming "go to date" all views jump to the target date, and cancelling keeps the current position.

features.name: Full lifecycle of an ordinary event
steps: Tap +
Events
Enter the title, location, and description
Set the start/end date and time, calendar, and color
Save
The event appears on the corresponding date
The month view shows a summary
The day view shows the complete information
After editing, all views sync
After deletion it disappears from all views at the same time
features.expected: After saving, the event must appear in all views of the selected date with consistent information; editing must sync to all views rather than creating copies; after deletion it disappears from all views and search at the same time; invalid times such as an end before the start should be rejected.

features.name: Converting between all-day and timed events
steps: Create an ordinary timed event
After enabling "all-day" the time input converts to a date range
After saving it appears at the top area of the day/week views
Then edit it into a timed event
The explicit start and end times are restored without incorrect date-range shifts
features.expected: All-day events must be stored as a date range and displayed at the top of the view without a specific time; when switching between the two types the date and end date must not shift or be lost; the displayed type is consistent across views.

features.name: Cross-day events
steps: Create an event such as 23:00–01:00 the next day
The month/day/week views correctly cover both dates
After enabling "show cross-midnight events in the top bar" the week-view layout changes with the setting
After editing the end time the occupied interval is recomputed
features.expected: A cross-midnight event must be marked on both dates with a correct duration (23:00→01:00 is about 2 hours); the top-bar display toggle must genuinely change the week-view presentation; after editing the end time the cross-day interval is recomputed in sync.

features.name: Recurring-event state machine
steps: Create an event
Set a daily/weekly/monthly or custom recurrence rule
The system generates future occurrences
Open one of the instances
Modifying a single instance or the whole series produces different results
Deleting a single occurrence must not delete the whole series
features.expected: Modifying a single instance affects only that occurrence while modifying the whole series affects all future ones; deleting a single occurrence must not delete the series; the recurrence rule must persist and expand future instances correctly in all views.

features.name: Recurring-event date boundaries
steps: Create recurring events such as "weekly" and "the Nth weekday of each month"
Calculations continue across months and years
Changing "week starts on" must not break the stored recurrence rules
The occurrence still falls on a reasonable date when months have different numbers of days
features.expected: Recurring instances must be generated continuously across months and years according to the rule with always-valid dates (e.g. the 31st of each month must not produce an invalid date in shorter months); changing "week starts on" must not break the stored recurrence rules.

features.name: Multiple event reminders and notification scheduling
steps: Create an event
Set a "10 minutes before" reminder
Add a second reminder at a different time
Save
Each reminder triggers at its own time
After changing the event time the notification trigger times are recomputed in sync
After deleting an event the related reminders are cancelled
features.expected: Multiple reminders must each trigger at their set times without overriding one another; after changing the event time the reminder times must be recomputed; deleting an event must cancel all its reminders without leaving stray notifications.

features.name: Global reminder-behavior configuration
steps: Change the notification sound stream, vibration, repeating notifications until dismissed, uniform delay time, delay duration, etc.
Subsequent notifications use the new rules
After a delay is applied to the notification it reminds again according to the configuration
The configuration is preserved after a restart
features.expected: Global reminder settings must apply to notifications of events created afterwards; after a delay is applied it must notify again at the configured time; the configuration persists across restarts and the options must not override one another.

features.name: New-event defaults
steps: Set the default start time, default duration, and default calendar, and enable "use the previous event's reminders as the new event's defaults"
Create a new event
The form automatically carries the corresponding default values
A user override changes only this instance; later creations still initialize from the configured rules
features.expected: The new-event form must prefill the start time, duration, and calendar according to the configuration; a one-time user override must not be written back to the defaults; with inheritance enabled, a new event should carry over the previous event's reminder settings.

features.name: Task creation and completion lifecycle
steps: Tasks
Enter the title and description
Set the date/time, reminders, recurrence, calendar, and task color
Save
The task appears on the corresponding date
Mark as complete
The state becomes completed
The presentation changes according to the "dim completed tasks" setting
The completed state is preserved after reopening
features.expected: After a task is completed its state must persist and be identifiable in the views; the "dim completed tasks" toggle should genuinely change the display; the completion state must not be lost after reopening or restarting.

features.name: Recurring tasks and task reminders
steps: Create a recurring task
Set the recurrence rule and reminders
Complete the current occurrence
The future occurrences still exist according to the rule
Completing the current instance must not permanently complete the whole recurring series
Due reminders trigger with the corresponding task instance
features.expected: Completing one instance may only mark that occurrence and future instances must continue to exist; task reminders must trigger at the corresponding instance's time; completing a single occurrence must not permanently mark the whole recurring series as done.

features.name: Events and tasks coexist
steps: Create an event and a task on the same day
Both are displayed while keeping their own types
Completing a task does not change the Event
Deleting an event does not affect Tasks
After disabling "allow creating tasks" the task-creation entry is hidden, but existing event data is unaffected
features.expected: Events and tasks must keep independent types and data, and operating on one must not affect the other; after disabling "allow creating tasks" the entry is hidden but existing task data is kept; the two object types are distinguishable in the views.

features.name: Multiple calendars and color ownership
steps: Create/manage multiple local calendars
Choose the target calendar when creating an Event/Task
Each calendar has its own color or resource attributes
After changing the calendar an object belongs to, the colors and categorization in the month/day views change in sync
When deleting a calendar, handle its entries according to the product rules
features.expected: An entry's color must be derived from its calendar, and the color and categorization update immediately after switching calendars; when deleting a calendar its entries must be handled according to the rules without leaving orphaned data; the calendar configuration must persist.

features.name: Event and task search
steps: Create several Events/Tasks with different titles, locations, and descriptions
Use the search at the top
Query by title to get matching results
Query by location/description to get the corresponding results
Tapping a result jumps to the corresponding date/object
Clearing the search restores the calendar view
features.expected: The search must cover fields such as title, location, and description and return real matches; tapping a result must jump to the corresponding date and object; clearing the query restores the original calendar view state.

features.name: Week/month view display configuration
steps: Change "week starts on", 24-hour format, highlight weekends, show week number, show grid, day start time, custom week-view days, etc.
Return to the calendar
The date arrangement, week numbers, timeline, and layout are re-rendered according to the configuration
The event date itself does not change
features.expected: Settings such as week start and 24-hour format must genuinely change the date arrangement and time display; event dates and data must not be changed by display settings; the configuration must persist and take effect consistently across views.

features.name: Event list and history window
steps: Set "show past events for 1 day/more"
The simple event list is recomputed for the window
After enabling description/location display or "replace the event description with the location" the list content changes
The original event data stays intact
features.expected: The event list must be filtered by the history window, and changing the number of days updates the list range in sync; options such as showing the description or location only change the presentation and must not alter or lose the original event data.

features.name: .ics export → import round trip
steps: Create several ordinary events, recurring events, and tasks
Export as .ics
Clean up / use a new environment
Import from .ics
Restore the representable fields such as title, date/time, description, location, recurrence rule, and reminders
The import result reappears on the correct dates. The official documentation explicitly supports .ics import/export, and the changelog also records task import/export and ICS compatibility fixes.
features.expected: The export must produce a valid .ics file; after importing, the titles, times, descriptions, locations, recurrence rules, and reminders must match the exported state and appear on the correct dates; recurring events must expand again according to the original rule.

features.name: Automatic backup and restore
steps: Enable automatic backup
After creating the backup, add/modify/delete several events and tasks
Restore from an old backup
The data returns to the backup point in time
The views, search results, and reminder schedules are rebuilt from the restored data
features.expected: After restoring, the events and tasks must return to the backup point in time without leftovers from additions or deletions made afterwards; the views, search, and reminders must be rebuilt from the restored data; the backup file must genuinely exist.

features.name: CalDAV calendar sync
steps: Enable CalDAV
Create/modify events locally
After syncing, the remote calendar is updated
After adding/modifying events remotely, sync again
Local view update
Recurring and all-day events keep reasonable date semantics. The official documentation explicitly supports CalDAV calendars such as Google Calendar, Outlook, and Nextcloud.
features.expected: Local changes must sync to the remote without creating duplicate events; remote changes must be reflected in the local views after the next sync; recurring and all-day events keep their original date semantics after a sync round trip.
